title: Ethereum Is Decentralized. Your Access Isn’t.
description:
Ethereum’s protocol can be decentralized, secure, and credibly neutral while most users never interact with it directly. Their path runs through wallets, RPCs, frontends, relays, indexers, identity systems, and increasingly AI agents, any of which can reintroduce trust, censorship, surveillance, or lock-in.

This talk starts with Moxie Marlinspike’s 2022 critique of Web3 and asks how much has actually changed. It then maps the user boundary where Ethereum’s guarantees still break and introduces the work being done within the Ethereum Foundation’s new Access Layer: private and verifiable reads, censorship-resistant transaction submission, safer account interfaces, privacy-preserving identity, bounded delegation, and credible fallback and exit paths.

Attendees will leave with a framework for understanding Ethereum’s remaining access-layer dependencies, the technologies being developed to remove them, and what a genuinely self-sovereign Ethereum experience could look like.
abstract:
Ethereum’s protocol is decentralized, but the way most people reach it isn’t: every balance check, signature or agent request usually depends on a few providers to tell the truth, answer and keep what you asked private.

This talk introduces the “zero option,” the idea that everything you do on Ethereum should have a credible way to do it without a single intermediary, and shows why it’s a ladder of steps rather than a choice between trusting a company and running your own node.

We’ll look at what the EF’s Access Layer is building to make independence easy and the default, including anon-RPC, clear signing, zkAPI and Kohaku, and where the ecosystem’s help is still needed.
